title: Fifth Word The Raw Recruit And The Lesson Of Duty And Prayer

questions.question: What kind of person is the untrained soldier shown to be at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: He is self-centered, overly focused on food and money, and careless about his real duty.

questions.question: What important responsibilities does he ignore?
questions.answer: He ignores military practice and fighting.

questions.question: What does he think about earning his food and supplies?
questions.answer: He thinks that is what really matters to him, so he keeps chasing it.

questions.question: What does he do when he goes after his livelihood?
questions.answer: He leaves the group and goes to the marketplace to shop.

questions.question: What does the trained soldier say is the other soldier’s true duty?
questions.answer: His true duty is to prepare himself and fight.

questions.question: Why does the trained soldier tell him to trust the king?
questions.answer: Because the king is responsible for feeding him and will not abandon him.

questions.question: What reason is given for why a person cannot fully provide for himself everywhere?
questions.answer: A person is weak and needy, so he cannot manage everything on his own.

questions.question: In a time of war, what could happen if the soldier refuses his duty?
questions.answer: He could be treated like a rebel and be punished.

questions.question: What are the two kinds of duties mentioned in the advice?
questions.answer: One belongs to the king, like providing food, and the other belongs to the soldiers, like training and fighting.

questions.question: In the comparison, what does the battlefield stand for?
questions.answer: It stands for the difficult and unstable life of this world.

questions.question: What does the regiment represent?
questions.answer: It represents the Muslim community of this age.

questions.question: Who does the good soldier represent?
questions.answer: He represents a practicing Muslim who fulfills religious duties and struggles against sin.

questions.question: Who does the careless soldier represent?
questions.answer: He represents a sinful person who becomes so busy with earning that he neglects worship and falls into wrongdoing.

questions.question: In the explanation of the comparison, what do training and instruction mainly stand for?
questions.answer: They mainly stand for the required prayers and worship.

questions.question: What is the “war” in the deeper meaning of the passage?
questions.answer: It is the struggle against the lower self, its desires, and the evil influences of devils among jinn and people.

questions.question: What is the goal of this struggle?
questions.answer: It is to protect the heart and soul from sin, bad character, and everlasting ruin.

questions.question: What is the first of the two main duties mentioned near the end of the passage?
questions.answer: It is giving life and providing what keeps it going.

questions.question: What is the second main duty?
questions.answer: It is worshipping, asking from, trusting in, and relying on Allah, the One who gives and sustains life.

questions.question: What main lesson does this whole comparison teach?
questions.answer: It teaches that a Muslim should not neglect worship and obedience while chasing worldly needs, because provision comes from Allah and our real duty is to serve Him.

questions.question: Why is the raw recruit criticized in this passage?
questions.answer: Because he makes his stomach and worldly needs more important than the job he was brought for.

questions.question: What wrong idea does he have about war and training?
questions.answer: He acts as if they are someone else’s concern and not his own responsibility.

questions.question: How does his behavior show misplaced priorities?
questions.answer: He leaves his post to shop and chase provision instead of doing his assigned duty.

questions.question: How does the disciplined soldier correct him?
questions.answer: He reminds him that his mission is to prepare and fight, not to run after food as if everything depends on him.

questions.question: According to the disciplined soldier, who has the duty of feeding the soldiers?
questions.answer: The king has that duty.

questions.question: Besides the king’s duty, what must the soldiers themselves do?
questions.answer: They must train and take part in the struggle they were assigned to.

questions.question: Why is relying only on oneself presented as a mistake?
questions.answer: Because human beings are weak and needy and cannot secure everything by their own power.

questions.question: What warning is given about ignoring duty during mobilization?
questions.answer: Such a person may be seen as disobedient and deserve punishment.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the lazy soldier if he refuses the good advice?
questions.answer: He will place himself in serious danger.

questions.question: When the comparison is explained, what does worldly life resemble?
questions.answer: It resembles a dangerous and unsettled war zone.

questions.question: In this explanation, who is the soldier with discipline and effort?
questions.answer: He is the believer who keeps up religious duties and fights against inner and outer evil.

questions.question: What inner enemies does that believer struggle against?
questions.answer: He struggles against his lower self and its desires.

questions.question: What outer enemies are also mentioned?
questions.answer: Evil influences from devils among jinn and human beings.

questions.question: How is the sinful person described in contrast?
questions.answer: He is described as someone drowned in earning a living, neglecting worship, and committing sins along the way.

questions.question: What serious spiritual mistake does that sinful person make while seeking provision?
questions.answer: He speaks and acts in a way that dishonors the true Provider.

questions.question: In the symbolic meaning, what do drills and lessons point to first of all?
questions.answer: They point to the prescribed prayers and acts of worship.

questions.question: What does victory in this “war” protect a person from?
questions.answer: It protects the heart and spirit from moral corruption and eternal loss.

questions.question: How are the two great duties divided between Allah and the servant?
questions.answer: Allah gives and sustains life, while the servant worships, asks from Him, and depends on Him.

questions.question: What balance between effort and trust is being taught?
questions.answer: A person should do the duty Allah assigned while trusting Allah for provision and support.

questions.question: What is the main problem with the inexperienced soldier’s attitude?
questions.answer: He cares more about comfort and food than about obedience and responsibility.

questions.question: What sentence sums up how he excuses himself from duty?
questions.answer: He treats military preparation and battle as if they are not his concern.

questions.question: What action shows that he lets worldly concerns pull him away from his mission?
questions.answer: He leaves the regiment and goes shopping in the market.

questions.question: How does the trained soldier describe the purpose for which they were brought there?
questions.answer: He says they were brought there to prepare and to fight.

questions.question: What does the trained soldier say about the king’s care for the soldiers?
questions.answer: He says the king will not leave them hungry because providing for them is his responsibility.

questions.question: Why does the advice mention human weakness and need?
questions.answer: To show that people should not act proudly as if they can secure everything by themselves.

questions.question: What consequence is mentioned for refusing one’s duty in wartime?
questions.answer: The person may be judged rebellious and punished.

questions.question: What are examples of the king’s side of responsibility?
questions.answer: Feeding the soldiers and taking care of their needs.

questions.question: What are examples of the soldiers’ side of responsibility?
questions.answer: Practice, readiness, and taking part in the struggle.

questions.question: What does the war-filled place stand for in real life?
questions.answer: It stands for the troubled life of this world.

questions.question: What does the regiment stand for in the explanation?
questions.answer: It stands for the Muslim community in the present age mentioned in the passage.

questions.question: What qualities belong to the Muslim represented by the good soldier?
questions.answer: He knows his duties, performs them, and works against sin and evil desires.

questions.question: What qualities belong to the person represented by the lazy soldier?
questions.answer: He becomes lost in earning, neglects worship, and falls into sinful behavior.

questions.question: What does the passage say this wrongdoer does toward the True Provider?
questions.answer: He shows disrespect by blaming or speaking wrongly while being consumed by worldly worries.

questions.question: What is the first meaning of training in the explanation?
questions.answer: It refers mainly to prayer and worship.

questions.question: Against what forces is the spiritual battle fought?
questions.answer: It is fought against the lower self, its cravings, and evil influences from jinn and people.

questions.question: What is meant by saving the heart and spirit?
questions.answer: It means protecting a person from sin, bad character, and final destruction in the next life.

questions.question: What final spiritual lesson is given about human duty?
questions.answer: Since Allah gives and sustains life, the servant should worship Him, ask from Him, trust Him, and rely on Him.

questions.question: What desire controls the raw recruit in the story?
questions.answer: His desire for food and worldly comfort controls him.

questions.question: What effect does that desire have on his behavior?
questions.answer: It makes him neglect preparation and run after material needs.

questions.question: Instead of staying with the regiment, where does he go?
questions.answer: He goes out to the market to buy things.

questions.question: What does his trained friend call him back to?
questions.answer: He calls him back to his real task of readiness and struggle.

questions.question: How does the friend connect trust with daily provision?
questions.answer: He teaches that the ruler takes responsibility for feeding those under his command.

questions.question: Why is the soldier told not to act as if everything depends on himself?
questions.answer: Because he is limited, needy, and unable to provide for himself in every place and situation.

questions.question: In the passage, what makes neglecting duty even more serious?
questions.answer: It is happening during a time of mobilization and war.

questions.question: What can happen to someone who ignores duty at such a time?
questions.answer: He may be considered mutinous and face punishment.

questions.question: How are the two categories of duty separated in the advice?
questions.answer: One category belongs to the ruler’s care, and the other belongs to the servant’s obedience and effort.

questions.question: What does the dangerous war setting symbolize?
questions.answer: It symbolizes the unstable and challenging life of this world.

questions.question: What does the organized army symbolize?
questions.answer: It symbolizes the Muslim society of the time mentioned.

questions.question: What kind of Muslim is represented by the responsible soldier?
questions.answer: A Muslim who fulfills obligations and strives against sinful impulses.

questions.question: What kind of person is represented by the other soldier?
questions.answer: A person so absorbed in worldly earning that he abandons religious responsibilities and slips into sin.

questions.question: What does the passage identify as the main form of spiritual training?
questions.answer: The required prayers and worship.

questions.question: How is the spiritual struggle described?
questions.answer: It is a fight against the lower self, selfish desires, and evil influences from both jinn and people.

questions.question: What is at stake in this struggle besides outward behavior?
questions.answer: The safety of the heart and soul is at stake.

questions.question: Which duty belongs to Allah according to the ending of the passage?
questions.answer: Giving life and sustaining it belongs to Allah.

questions.question: Which duty belongs to human beings?
questions.answer: Worshipping, asking from Allah, and trusting in Him belongs to human beings.

questions.question: What overall correction does this passage make to a person’s thinking?
questions.answer: It corrects the idea that chasing provision is the main purpose of life and teaches that worship and reliance on Allah come first.

questions.question: What false priority does the careless soldier give himself?
questions.answer: He treats getting food and worldly gain as more important than discipline and service.

questions.question: How does he speak about the main mission he was given?
questions.answer: He dismisses it as someone else’s business.

questions.question: What does he spend his time pursuing?
questions.answer: He spends it chasing his livelihood and shopping.

questions.question: What central reminder does his companion give him?
questions.answer: He reminds him that he was brought there for training and fighting.

questions.question: What does the companion teach about who provides food?
questions.answer: He teaches that the ruler is in charge of feeding those under his authority.

questions.question: Why should the soldier not be overconfident in his own ability to provide?
questions.answer: Because he is weak and dependent, not fully self-sufficient.

questions.question: What danger comes from refusing one’s duty in wartime?
questions.answer: It can lead to being counted as rebellious and deserving punishment.

questions.question: What does the companion say about the two duties in their situation?
questions.answer: One is the ruler’s responsibility to provide, and the other is the soldiers’ responsibility to serve.

questions.question: How does the passage invite the reader to judge the lazy soldier’s path?
questions.answer: It says his path clearly puts him in danger.

questions.question: In the explained meaning, what does the war zone refer to?
questions.answer: It refers to the troubled conditions of worldly life.

questions.question: In that same explanation, what does the regiment refer to?
questions.answer: It refers to the Muslim community of the century mentioned in the passage.

questions.question: What does the good soldier show about a faithful Muslim?
questions.answer: A faithful Muslim learns and performs religious duties and resists sin.

questions.question: What spiritual enemies must such a Muslim oppose?
questions.answer: He must oppose his lower self, its desires, and devils from jinn and mankind.

questions.question: What makes the other type of person spiritually dangerous?
questions.answer: He becomes swallowed by worldly work and leaves worship and moral boundaries behind.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does he do while trying to earn?
questions.answer: He neglects obligations and commits sins that come before him.

questions.question: What practice is put at the center of spiritual instruction?
questions.answer: The prescribed prayers are placed at the center.

questions.question: What does the spiritual battle seek to rescue?
questions.answer: It seeks to rescue the heart and spirit from eternal destruction.

questions.question: What truth about life and worship closes the passage?
questions.answer: The One who gives and sustains life is the One who should be worshipped, asked from, trusted, and relied on.

questions.question: What is one strong lesson an 8th-grade Muslim student can take from this passage?
questions.answer: School, work, and daily needs matter, but they should not make us forget salah, obedience to Allah, and the struggle against sin.

questions.question: At the start of the passage, what is the raw recruit mainly concerned about?
questions.answer: He is mainly concerned about his appetite and making sure he gets what he wants.

questions.question: What serious things does he neglect because of that?
questions.answer: He neglects preparation and the struggle he is supposed to join.

questions.question: What does he do outside the regiment?
questions.answer: He goes to the market to look after his own worldly needs.

questions.question: What does the trained soldier say is the recruit’s assigned purpose?
questions.answer: He says the recruit’s purpose there is to train and fight.

questions.question: How does the trained soldier encourage reliance on the king?
questions.answer: He says the king is responsible for feeding him and will not leave him starving.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about human ability to secure provision alone?
questions.answer: It teaches that people are too weak and needy to depend only on themselves.

questions.question: Why is this neglect especially blameworthy in the story?
questions.answer: Because it happens during a period of war when obedience matters even more.

questions.question: What official response could follow such neglect?
questions.answer: The person could be treated as disobedient and punished.

questions.question: What is one duty that belongs to the king in the example?
questions.answer: Providing food and care is one of the king’s duties.

questions.question: What is one duty that belongs to the soldiers?
questions.answer: Training and taking part in the fight is one of their duties.

questions.question: When the meaning is explained, what does the battlefield become a symbol for?
questions.answer: It becomes a symbol for this unstable worldly life.

questions.question: What real group does the regiment represent?
questions.answer: It represents the Muslim community in this era spoken of in the passage.

questions.question: What real person does the disciplined soldier represent?
questions.answer: He represents a devout Muslim who keeps his obligations and struggles against evil.

questions.question: What real person does the neglectful soldier represent?
questions.answer: He represents a sinner who gets lost in earning and leaves religious duties behind.

questions.question: What two wrong results come from that sinful lifestyle?
questions.answer: The person neglects obligations and falls into sins.

questions.question: In the explanation, what is the first meaning of military training?
questions.answer: It means the daily prayers and worship.

questions.question: What must be fought in the inner and outer struggle?
questions.answer: A person must fight against selfish desires and evil influences from both unseen beings and people.

questions.question: What is the purpose of winning that struggle?
questions.answer: It is to save the heart and soul from sin, bad morals, and everlasting ruin.

questions.question: How does the passage define the right response to the One who gives life?
questions.answer: The right response is to worship Him, ask Him for help, trust Him, and rely on Him.
